title: Quarter-End Growth Push
summary: A large SME loan pipeline can help close the quarter, but several files have incomplete verification trails.
facts: Sales leadership is pushing for same-day sanction.
Two files have missing income-supporting annexures.
Competitors are approving similar deals aggressively.
coachingTip: Reward participants who preserve growth but insist on documented conditional controls.

title: Suspicious Vendor Onboarding
summary: A strategic vendor offers deep discounts, but KYC metadata and sanction screening have conflicting records.
facts: Procurement says delay will affect a launch milestone.
Vendor address and bank account ownership mismatch in two systems.
coachingTip: Strong answers explain why escalations protect the business from downstream disruption.

title: AI Collections Assistant Rollout
summary: The business wants to launch an AI collections assistant before the audit window closes, but explainability is limited.
facts: Pilot results show 18% improvement in recovery calls.
Model logs do not fully capture prompt-to-decision reasoning.
Customer advocacy team worries about fairness complaints.
coachingTip: Top scores should go to participants who propose a staged release with controls.

title: Cross-Border Payment Exception
summary: A premium client needs an urgent cross-border release, but the transaction pattern deviates from normal behavior.
facts: Relationship manager says the client may leave if delayed.
The beneficiary country risk score increased last week.
Manual review can still happen within four hours.
coachingTip: Reward decisions that prioritize review rather than instant release.

title: Low-Friction Digital Onboarding
summary: Product wants to remove one verification step to improve drop-off, but fraud monitoring is not fully tuned.
facts: Current funnel drop-off is 27% at the identity proof step.
Fraud team expects a temporary increase in false positives.
Leadership wants a visible win before the town hall.
coachingTip: Strong players preserve conversion gains while adding fallback checks.

title: Model Drift in Credit Scoring
summary: A credit scoring model still meets business SLAs, but drift indicators and segment bias warnings have increased.
facts: Collections success has improved in two profitable segments.
A governance review is due next week.
One regional cluster shows materially worse approval parity.
coachingTip: The best responses balance business continuity with immediate safeguards.
